title: Rapid-cycle triage and surge staffing protocol for emergency scope pruning and continuity lanes
creator: Rajat Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood's engineering and product teams need a compact, operational protocol to handle mid-cycle disruptions that require immediate scope reductions, temporary staff surges, or rerouting of critical work into continuity lanes. Current guidance is scattered across playbooks and past retros; teams reported uncertainty during the last two emergent incidents (Q4 2025 scaling regression + customer security audit).

Goal:
Create a practical runbook and decision framework for product cycles that: 1) enables rapid, fair scope pruning with documented criteria; 2) defines a staffing surge protocol with roles and timeboxes; and 3) establishes continuity lanes for low-risk, high-visibility features so SLAs and key OKRs are protected.

Success metrics (how we'll know this helps):
- Time to decision for emergency scope cuts reduced from median 48h to <= 12h.
- Clear surge staffing rostering practiced in at least two teams during next cycle.
- Post-incident blameless review shows fewer ad-hoc prioritization escalations.

Scope (what this ticket delivers):
- One-pager decision tree for scope triage (criteria: customer impact, security/regulatory risk, unblocker status, revenue/OKR delta).
- Surge staffing protocol (roles: surge captain, scope owner, triage liaison, backfill engineer) with suggested timeboxes and handoffs.
- Prescriptive continuity lane definition (what goes into lane vs. what is paused).
- Communication templates for customers and internal stakeholders (status, ETA, rollback option).
- Example runbook filled with two real-cycle scenarios (payment-affecting regression; data-privacy audit) and recommended actions.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting cycle-level prioritization policy (this is complementary).
- Team-specific capacity planning per se; we'll provide templates and examples only.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Staffing surges can pull up to 20% of Engineering capacity from non-critical work for a 2-week window (governed by Eng lead sign-off).
- Legal/Security escalations always take precedence and have separate SLA.
- We will align with Revenue/Support when customer-impact criteria are considered.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Maya Chen (assignee), Rajat Kapoor (creator), Sasha Rivera (PM lead)
- Eng: Engineering Managers for serving/runtime teams; ENG-1842 primary dependency
- Design: DES-98 for comms templates and dashboard updates
- GTM/Support: informal review for external messaging

Rollout plan:
1) Draft runbook and decision tree (this ticket).
2) Dry run with two volunteer squads during next planning sprint; capture friction points.
3) Revise and publish in Confluence + add a shortcut in Console operations docs.
4) Host a 30-min cross-functional walkthrough and a 1-hr tabletop simulation for PM/Eng/Design leads.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runbook published and linked from CycleOps home doc.
- Two teams run the dry-run and file feedback in this ticket (comments).
- Templates added to the cycle planning template repo (link below).
- Playbook acknowledged by Eng leadership and PM leadership.

Links and references:
- Existing capacity playbooks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/cycle/capacity-playbooks
- Incident examples (Q4 2025): https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/q4-2025-scaling-regression.pdf
- Cycle planning template repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cycle-templates

Notes: This deliverable intentionally prioritizes speed and ease-of-use; it should be usable in a 10–15 minute read by an on-call PM or Eng lead.
